1.note: Solomon speaks to Yahweh as if he were speaking to someone else to show that he respects Yahweh. Alternate translation: [Yahweh, you have said that you]
Here the word “thick” shows that the darkness is extreme. Yahweh spoke of not allowing sinful people to see him as if he were to live in darkness. Alternate translation: [in great darkness]

2.q: I have built you a lofty residence
2.note: Solomon speaks of commanding the people to build the temple and telling them how to do it as if he himself had built it. Alternate translation: [I and your people have built you a lofty residence]
a magnificent house, appropriate for someone who is very important

3.q: while all the assembly of Israel was standing
3.note: The phrase “all the assembly” is a generalization. It does not mean that every person of Israel was standing, but that all of the people who were gathered there were standing. Alternate translation: [while the people of Israel there were standing]

4.q: May Yahweh, the God of Israel, be praised
4.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Praise Yahweh, the God of Israel]
King Solomon actually was one of King David’s sons.
“has caused it to happen.” The word “it” refers to what God had promised. Alternate translation: [has ensured that he fulfilled his promises]
The hand is a metonym for power. Alternate translation: [by his own power]

5.q: in order for my name to be there
5.note: Here the metonym “my name” represents Yahweh’s reputation, and his name being there represents people recognizing his greatness and worshiping him there. Alternate translation: [for people to worship me there]

5.q: to be prince over my people Israel
5.note: Being “prince over people” represents ruling them. Alternate translation: [to rule my people Israel]

6.q: so that my name might be there
6.note: Here the metonym “my name” represents Yahweh’s reputation, and his name being there represents people recognizing his greatness and worshiping him there. Alternate translation: [so that people might worship me there]

6.q: to be over my people Israel
6.note: Being “over” people represents ruling them. Alternate translation: [to rule my people Israel]

7.note:
# Connecting Statement:

King Solomon continues speaking to the people at the temple.

7.q: it was in the heart of David my father
7.note: Here David’s heart is spoken of as if it were a container, and what he desired is spoken of as if it were an item in the container. Alternate translation: [David my father desired]
This could mean: (1) Yahweh’s name represents himself. Alternate translation: [for Yahweh … for me] or (2) Yahweh’s name represents his reputation. Alternate translation: [for Yahweh’s reputation]

8.q: it was in your heart … for it to be in your heart
8.note: Here David’s heart is spoken of as if it were a container, and what he desired is spoken of as if it were an item in the container. Alternate translation: [you desired … to desire to do that]
This could mean: (1) Yahweh’s name represents himself. Alternate translation: [for me] or (2) Yahweh’s name represents his reputation. Alternate translation: [for my reputation]

8.q: In that it was in your heart
8.note: Alternate translation: [Because it was in your heart] or [Because you wanted]

9.q: one who will come from your loins
9.note: Alternate translation: [one who will be your own offspring] or [one whom you yourself will father]

10.q: has carried out the word that he had said
10.note: This is an idiom. Alternate translation: [has done exactly what he said he would do]

10.q: I have arisen in the place of David my father
10.note: Height is a metaphor for power. Alternate translation: [I have gained the power that David my father had]

10.q: I sit on the throne of Israel
10.note: The throne is a metonym for the activity of the one who sits on the throne. Alternate translation: [I rule over Israel]
This could mean: (1) Yahweh’s name represents himself. Alternate translation: [for Yahweh] or (2) Yahweh’s name represents his reputation. Alternate translation: [for the reputation of Yahweh]

11.q: in which is Yahweh’s covenant, which
11.note: The stone tablets on which Yahweh had written the terms of the covenant are spoken of as if they were the covenant itself. Alternate translation: [in which are the tablets on which Yahweh wrote the terms of the covenant that]

12.q: in the presence of all the assembly of Israel
12.note: Alternate translation: [in front of the people of Israel who had gathered there]
“raised his hands.” This was to show that he was praying.

13.q: five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high
13.note: You may convert these to modern measures. Alternate translation: [two and one-third meters long, two and one-third meters wide, and one and one-half meters high]

13.q: he spread out his hands toward the heavens
13.note: Solomon lifted up his hands and held them high as he knelt on the platform to pray. Spreading out his hands toward the heavens was a way of showing that he was praying to Yahweh.

14.q: on the earth, who keeps covenant and steadfast love with your servants
14.note: This can be stated as a new sentence. Alternate translation: [on the earth. You keep your promise to love your servants] or [on the earth. You faithfully love your servants]

14.q: walk before you with all their heart
14.note: The way a person lives is spoken of as if that person were walking on a path. Alternate translation: [live wholeheartedly the way that you want them to]

15.q: you who have kept with your servant David my father, what you promised him
15.note: “you who have kept your promise to your servant David my father.” To keep a promise is an idiom that means to do what one has promised. Alternate translation: [you who have done what you promised your servant David my father]
The phrase “with your mouth” may emphasize that God himself spoke. It was not someone else who made the promise. Alternate translation: [you yourself spoke]

15.q: and have fulfilled it with your hand
15.note: The hand is a metonym for the power of the hand. Alternate translation: [and, by your power, have fulfilled what you said] or [and by your power have done what you said]
This refers to the day when Solomon was saying this prayer.

16.note:
# Connecting Statement:

King Solomon continues praying.

16.q: carry out what you have promised
16.note: This is a request. To carry out what one has said is an idiom meaning to do what one has said. Alternate translation: [please do what you have promised]

16.q: You will not fail to have a man
16.note: God speaking in terms of David having a man implies that the man would be a descendant of David. This can be stated positively. Alternate translation: [you will always have a descendant] (See also: [Double Negatives](ta:figs-doublenegatives))

16.q: a man in my sight to sit on the throne of Israel
16.note: The phrase “in my sight” here implies that God would choose the man and the man would want to obey God.

16.q: to sit on the throne of Israel
16.note: The throne is a metonym for the activity of the one who sits on the throne. Alternate translation: [to rule over Israel]

16.q: to walk in my law, as you have walked before me
16.note: The way a person behaves is spoken of as if that person were walking on a path. Alternate translation: [to obey my law, as you have obeyed me] or [to be faithful to my law as you have been faithful to me]

17.q: let your word be confirmed, which you have spoken to your servant David
17.note: Alternate translation: [I want you to make come true the word that you have spoken to your servant David]
This can be translated in active form. Alternate translation: [confirm your word] or [make your word come true]

18.note:
# Connecting Statement:

King Solomon continues praying.

18.q: But will God actually live with mankind on the earth?
18.note: Possible meanings of this question are: (1) Solomon is asking a real question and expecting an answer or (2) the question is rhetorical and Solomon is emphasizing that God is too big and mighty to live on earth. Alternate translation: [But it surely cannot be that God will actually live on the earth!]
Here Solomon speaks about God in the third person to show his great respect for God. It can be stated in the second person. Alternate translation: [But will you]
Here “Look” indicates that he is about to say something important.

18.q: you—how much less can this temple that I have built
18.note: Alternate translation: [you, so this temple that I have built certainly cannot contain you]

18.q: this temple that I have built
18.note: Solomon speaks of commanding the people to build the temple and telling them how to do it as if he himself had built it. Alternate translation: [this temple that your people have built under my leadership] or [this house that I and your people have built]

19.q: respect this prayer of your servant and his request
19.note: The words “prayer” and “request” mean basically the same thing and emphasize that he is sincere as he makes his request. Solomon refers to himself as “your servant” to show that he respects Yahweh. This can be stated in first person. Alternate translation: [respect me, your servant, as I make this request] (See also: [First, Second or Third Person](ta:figs-123person))

19.q: listen to the cry and prayer that your servant prays before you
19.note: The words “cry” and “prayer” mean basically the same thing and emphasize that he is sincere as he asks Yahweh to help him. Solomon refers to himself as “your servant” to show that he respects Yahweh. This can be stated in first person. Alternate translation: [listen to me, your servant, as I call for you to help me] (See also: [First, Second or Third Person](ta:figs-123person))

20.q: May your eyes be open toward this temple
20.note: The eyes being open is a metonym for watching, and here watching represents protecting. “Please watch over this temple” or “Please protect this temple”
This is a merism. Alternate translation: [all the time] or [continually]

20.q: where you promised to put your name
20.note: This could mean: (1) Yahweh’s name represents himself. Alternate translation: [where you promised to be] or (2) Yahweh’s name represents his reputation. Alternate translation: [where you promised to make people know you]

20.q: the prayer your servant prays toward this place
20.note: Solomon refers to himself as “your servant” to show that he respects Yahweh. This can be stated in first person. Alternate translation: [the prayer that I, your servant, pray toward this place]

21.note:
# Connecting Statement:

King Solomon continues praying.

21.q: So listen to the requests of your servant and of your people Israel
21.note: Solomon speaks of himself as “your servant” to show that he respects Yahweh. This can be stated in first person. Alternate translation: [So listen to my requests and the requests of your people Israel]
Alternate translation: [when you hear our prayers, please forgive our sins]

22.note:
# Connecting Statement:

King Solomon continues praying.

22.q: is required to swear an oath
22.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [someone requires him to swear an oath]

23.q: bringing what he has done upon his own head
23.note: To bring someone’s conduct on him represents punishing him for his bad conduct. Alternate translation: [punishing him as he deserves]
Here the “head” refers to the whole person. Alternate translation: [on him]

23.q: give to him according to his righteousness
23.note: Alternate translation: [give him what he deserves because he is innocent]

24.q: When your people Israel are defeated by an enemy
24.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [When an enemy defeats your people Israel]

24.q: because they have sinned against you
24.note: Alternate translation: [because your people Israel have sinned against you]

24.q: if they turn back to you
24.note: Here “turn back to you” represents submitting again to God. Alternate translation: [if they submit to you again]
This could mean: (1) “confess that they have sinned against you” or (2) “praise you” or (3) “say that they will obey you from now on.”
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **forgiveness**, you can express the same idea with a verbal form. Alternate translation: [ask you to forgive them]

25.note: To “listen” is an idiom for responding to prayer. Alternate translation: [please honor their prayer] or [please answer their prayer]

25.q: bring them back to the land that you gave to them and to their ancestors
25.note: This implies that when their enemies defeated them, God’s people will have gone to live in other lands. Alternate translation: [bring them back to their own land]

26.q: When the skies are shut up and there is no rain
26.note: The sky is spoken of as if it were a building in which God stores the rain, and when God does not want it to rain he closes the door to the building. Alternate translation: [When you do not allow rain to fall from the skies]
This could mean: (1) “confess that they have sinned against you” or (2) “praise you” or (3) “say that they will obey you from now on.”
Here “turn from” is a metaphor for stopping doing it. Alternate translation: [stop committing their sins] or [stop acting sinfully]

27.q: the good way in which they should walk
27.note: The way a person lives is spoken of as if that person were walking on a path. Alternate translation: [the good way that they should live]

27.q: your land, which you have given to your people as an inheritance
27.note: The land is spoken of as if it were an inheritance because God wanted them to possess it forever. Alternate translation: [your land, which you have given to your people to own forever]

28.note: These are agricultural terms that refer to the death of crops from either too little or too much rain, respectively.
A “locust” is a type of grasshopper that causes destruction by eating crops. The word “caterpillar” refers to an early growth stage of the locust.

29.note: The words “prayers” and “requests” mean basically the same thing and emphasize that the person is sincere as he makes his requests.

29.q: knowing the plague and sorrow in his own heart
29.note: Here “plague” is a metaphor for sin, and sin and sorrow are spoken of as being in people’s hearts. Alternate translation: [knowing the sin and sorrow in his own heart]

29.q: he spreads out his hands toward this temple
29.note: This was a way of showing that they were praying to the God of the temple. See how you translated “spread out his hands” in 2 Chronicles 6:12.

30.note: Here “his ways” represents the person’s behavior. Alternate translation: [for what he has done]

31.q: so that they may walk in your ways
31.note: Here “walk in your ways” represents living and behaving the way God wants. Alternate translation: [so that they may live as you want them to]

32.note:
# Connecting Statement:

King Solomon continues praying.

32.q: who—because of your great name, your mighty hand, and your outstretched arm—comes
32.note: It is implied that the foreigners come because they hear about God’s greatness. Alternate translation: [who hears about your great name, your mighty hand, and your outstretched arm—if he comes]
Here God’s name represents his reputation. Alternate translation: [your great reputation] or [your greatness]

32.q: your mighty hand, and your outstretched arm
32.note: These two phrases mean basically the same thing and refer to God’s power. (See also: [Metonymy](ta:figs-metonymy))
Praying toward Yahweh’s temple shows that one is praying to Yahweh.

33.note: Here God’s name represents his reputation. Alternate translation: [may know your reputation] or [may know your greatness]

33.q: as do your own people Israel
33.note: Alternate translation: [as your own people Israel know your name and fear you]

33.q: this house I have built is called by your name
33.note: The phrase “is called by your name” shows that God possesses and owns the house. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [you own this house that I have built]

Solomon speaks of commanding the people to build the temple and telling them how to do it as if he himself had built it. See how you translated a similar phrase in 2 Chronicles 6:18. Alternate translation: [this house that your people have built under my leadership] or [this house that I and your people have built]

34.note:
# Connecting Statement:

King Solomon continues praying.

34.q: Suppose that your people go out … suppose that they pray
34.note: When Solomon was speaking, these hypothetical situations had not happened, but Solomon knew that they might happen in the future. Use the form in your language for talking about events that have not happened but might happen in the future.

34.q: they pray to you toward this city … and toward the house
34.note: Praying toward Jerusalem and the temple shows that they are praying to Yahweh.

34.q: the house that I have built
34.note: Solomon speaks of commanding the people to build the temple and telling them how to do it as if he himself had built it. Alternate translation: [this house that your people have built under my leadership] or [this house that I and your people have built]
This could mean: (1) Yahweh’s name represents himself. Alternate translation: [for you] or (2) Yahweh’s name represents his reputation. Alternate translation: [for your reputation]

35.note: The abstract nouns “prayer” and “request” can be stated as verbs. Alternate translation: [to what they request when they pray to you]
This refers to helping them fight against their enemies.

36.note:
# Connecting Statement:

King Solomon continues praying.

36.q: Suppose they sin … suppose that you are angry
36.note: When Solomon was speaking, these hypothetical situations had not happened, but Solomon knew that they might happen in the future. Use the form in your language for talking about events that have not happened but might happen in the future.

36.q: hand them over to the enemy
36.note: Here “hand them over to the enemy” represents allowing the enemy to capture them.

36.q: so that the enemy carries them away
36.note: Here “carries them away” represents forcing them to leave their own country. Alternate translation: [so that the enemy forces them to leave]

37.q: suppose they realize … suppose that they repent … Suppose that they say
37.note: When Solomon was speaking, these hypothetical situations had not happened, but Solomon knew that they might happen in the future. Use the form in your language for talking about events that have not happened but might happen in the future.

If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [where their enemies have taken them as exiles]
Alternate translation: [beg you to be merciful to them]

37.q: We have acted perversely and sinned. We have behaved wickedly
37.note: These two sentences mean the same thing. Together they emphasize how bad the people’s actions were.
The words mean basically the same thing and emphasize how badly the people sinned.

38.q: Suppose that they return … suppose that they pray
38.note: When Solomon was speaking, these hypothetical situations had not happened, but Solomon knew that they might happen in the future. Use the form in your language for talking about events that have not happened but might happen in the future.
Here “return to you” represents submitting to Yahweh again. Alternate translation: [they submit to you again]

38.q: with all their heart and with all their soul
38.note: The idioms “with all their heart” means “completely” and “with all their soul” means “with all their being.” These two phrases have similar meanings. Alternate translation: [completely] (See also: [Doublet](ta:figs-doublet))

38.q: where they took them as captives
38.note: Alternate translation: [where their enemies took them as captives]

38.q: that they pray toward their land
38.note: This refers to Israel. Praying toward Israel would show that they were praying to Yahweh, the God of Israel. Alternate translation: [that they pray facing their land]

38.q: toward the city that you chose
the house that I have built
38.note: Solomon speaks of commanding the people to build the temple and telling them how to do it as if he himself had built it. Alternate translation: [the house that your people have built under my leadership] or [the house that I and your people have built]
This could mean: (1) Yahweh’s name represents himself. Alternate translation: [for you] or (2) Yahweh’s name represents his reputation. Alternate translation: [for your reputation]

39.q: to their prayer and to their requests
39.note: The words “prayer” and “requests” mean basically the same thing and emphasize that the people are sincere as they make their requests. Alternate translation: [their requests]

40.note: Here the word “now” is used to draw attention to the important point that follows.
The eyes being open is a metonym for seeing. Here it represents looking attentively. Alternate translation: [please pay attention to us] or [please look at us]

40.q: let your ears be attentive to the prayer
40.note: The ears being attentive is a metonym for listening attentively. Alternate translation: [please listen to the prayer]

40.q: to the prayer that is made in this place
40.note: This can be expressed in active form. Alternate translation: [to the prayer that we make in this place] or [to us as we pray to you in this place]

41.q: arise, Yahweh God, to your resting place
41.note: This pictures God as if he were sitting on his throne, and asks that he will get up from his throne and come to this place. Alternate translation: [arise, Yahweh God, and come to your resting place]
Alternate translation: [the ark, which is a symbol of your power]

41.q: Let your priests … be clothed with salvation
41.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **salvation**, you can express the same idea with a verbal form such as “to save.” This could mean: (1) being clothed with salvation is a metaphor for experiencing salvation. Alternate translation: [Let your priests … know that you have saved them] or (2) being clothed with salvation is a metaphor for demonstrating salvation. Alternate translation: [Let your priests … demonstrate how you save people] (See also: [Abstract Nouns](ta:figs-abstractnouns))

42.q: do not turn the face of your anointed away from you
42.note: Turning the face of someone away represents rejecting him. Alternate translation: [do not reject your anointed one]

“your anointed one.” Being anointed is a metonym for being chosen by God. King Solomon may have been speaking specifically about himself. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the one you anointed] or [me, the one you chose to be king] (See also: [Active or Passive](ta:figs-activepassive))

42.q: Keep in mind your acts of covenant loyalty for David, your servant
42.note: The phrase “your acts” can be expressed with the phrase “what you have done.” Alternate translation: [Remember what you have done for David, your servant, because of your covenant loyalty]
